deities: Keshavdeva (Lord Krishna, presiding deity of the complex)

history.dynasty: Ancient (tradition: Vajranabha; Gupta: Chandragupta II, 400 CE; Gahadavala-era rebuild 1150 CE; Bundela: Raja Veer Singh Deva, 1618); modern (Dalmia and Birla industrialist families; Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sansthan, founded 1951)
history.period: Site ancient (archaeological finds from the 6th century BCE); the modern Keshavdeva temple was built 29 June 1957-6 September 1958 (inaugurated by Hanuman Prasad Poddar); the wider complex was built 1953-1982
history.summary: RELATED RECORD: the Keshavdeva Temple is the principal Krishna shrine of the Shri Krishna Janmasthan complex at Katra Keshavdeo - seq 2390 (Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple, not yet processed at the time of writing) documents the same complex, so keep these records linked but separate. The complex contains three temples: the Keshavdeva temple dedicated to Krishna, the Garbha Griha shrine marking the prison cell believed to be Krishna's birthplace (against the rear wall of the Shahi Eidgah), and the Bhagavata Bhavan (deities installed 12 February 1982) with five shrines including Radha-Krishna, Balarama-Subhadra-Jagannatha and Rama-Lakshmana-Sita. Site history: tradition attributes a first temple to Krishna's great-grandson Vajranabha; a Vaishnava temple may date to the 1st century; Chandragupta II rebuilt it in 400 CE; Mahmud of Ghazni plundered it in 1017/1018; a Vishnu temple was built here in 1150 (Vikram Samvat 1207) by Jajja; Sikandar Lodi destroyed Mathura's temples in the 16th century; Raja Veer Singh Deva Bundela built a magnificent temple in 1618 at a cost of Rs 33 lakh (described by Tavernier in 1650 and patronised by Dara Shikoh); Aurangzeb destroyed the Keshavdeva temple in 1670 and built the Shahi Eidgah on its plinth (confirmed in ASI's 1920 gazette notifications cited in a 2024 RTI reply). The land was auctioned by the East India Company in 1815 and bought by Raja Patnimal of Banaras; Madan Mohan Malaviya acquired it in 1944, and Jugal Kishore Birla formed the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Trust (registered 1951 as Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sansthan); construction by Ramkrishna Dalmia and Jaidayal Dalmia ran from October 1953 to February 1982, funded by the Dalmia and Birla families among others. The Keshavdeva Temple itself stands south of the Shahi Eidgah and was built by Ramkrishna Dalmia in memory of his mother Jadiadevi Dalmia. NOTE: older scholarly sources sometimes describe the pre-1670 complex as the Bindraban/Veer Singh temple; the 'destroyed by Ghazni in 1018, by Lodi in the 16th century' sequence follows standard modern accounts - verify details locally.

name: Kesava Deo Temple
town_description: Mathura is an ancient city on the banks of the Yamuna in the Braj region, revered as the birthplace of Lord Krishna and counted among Hinduism's Sapta Puri (seven holy cities). A major pilgrimage centre for millennia, it is dotted with temples, ghats and kunds, and lies about 160 km south-east of Delhi on the Delhi-Agra corridor.

travel.airport: Kheria Airport, Agra, about 60 km from Mathura; Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi, about 160 km.
travel.railway: Mathura Junction - the Janmasthan complex is in Govind Nagar, a short drive from the station.
travel.road: On Deeg Marg near Deeg Gate Chouraha, Mathura 281001; city auto-rickshaws and taxis; buses from Delhi and Agra.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami is the grandest festival but extremely crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published in the consulted sources for this temple specifically - typical Janmasthan complex timings are a morning session and an evening session; verify locally before travel.
